title: Appeal of Tan v. Houston Metro Presbytery
disposition_detail: The Standing Judicial Commission found the appeal judicially out of order because Tan had not submitted to a regular trial as required by BCO 42-2. It did not decide the merits.
first_summary: The SJC dismissed Tan’s appeal because he had not submitted to a regular trial as required by BCO 42-2. The brief decision did not address the merits.
summary: Tan attempted to appeal without first submitting to a regular trial. The SJC found the appeal judicially out of order under BCO 42-2 and therefore did not reach its merits. Although the source header labels the disposition “dismissed,” the adopted judgment expressly classifies it as judicially out of order.
